finding: The process-level go878 raw-generation backpressure patch is liveness-unsafe on the exact current architecture because tools/run_6000_free_swarm_fast.py installs free_swarm_backfill_scheduler into the same 6000 fabric. pending_extraction is included in the pressure term used by the patcher, so stopping the 6000 process under high pending-extraction pressure can stop the only observed historical extraction transport that would drain that pressure.
hypothesis: A liveness-preserving conversion controller should separate raw-generation admission from historical-conversion transport. While pending extraction exists, the fabric must remain alive and raw-only slots should be reduced or eliminated at prompt/scheduler level; process-level stop may be considered only when the remaining pressure is not carried by that process.
counterhypothesis: A separate independently active historical extraction transport could make process-level stop safe, but no such active extraction transport was observed in the inspected supervisor/fabric chain. Exact runtime process inventory is still required before promoting the stronger claim that the 6000 fabric is the sole extractor.
